title: wbab3m
The Harre case .
hook: After Karbala, Yazid's army sacked the Prophet's city for three days, then stoned the Kaaba with hammers.
scenes.0.text: After Karbala, Medina was still mourning the Prophet's grandson. Yazid's governor of Medina, his uncle's son Uthman b. Muhammad b. It was Abi Sufyan. The governor sent a delegation of the city elders to Damascus, to the palace of Yazid. The delegation was headed by **Abdullah b. Hanzala**. His father, Hanzala, was martyred in Uhud and was mentioned as a companion whose body was washed by angels. He welcomed the Yazidi delegation and gave them great gifts. Abdullah b. He made a donation of about one hundred thousand dirhams to Hanzala. But the delegation couldn't forget what they saw in the palace. When they returned to their people, they said, "We have come to a man who has no religion. He drinks wine, plays drums, and his maids sing and play with his dogs. We have made him a caliphate. They also told me that Yazid didn't pray on time because he was drunk. Mes'udi writes that Yazid was fond of fun, birds of prey, dogs, monkeys and drinking parties. The people of Abdullah b. He reminded Hanzala that Yazid was offering him a treat. And he said, "Yes, he did. But I only took it so I could find the strength to fight him. I will fight against him with my sons". The people of Medina broke their pledge to Yazid and Abdullah b. He has vowed to Hanzala.

scenes.1.text: The Medinans appointed Yazid's governor and the sons of Umayyad in the city as Mervan b. He's surrounded the judge's house. The besieged wrote a letter to Damascus and asked for help: "Enough, enough!" When the letter reached Yazid, he was sitting with his feet in a pool of water because of the pain in his feet. He read the letter and became angry. Yazid's eyes weren't just on Medina. Abdullah b. Zubair did not give him a bequest in Mecca. Yazid wrote to Ubaydullah b. Ziyad in Kufa that Ibn Zubair should march on him. Even Ibn Ziyad, who martyred Husayn at Karbala, rejected this order and said, "I will not do both at once for this pervert. I will not kill the son of the daughter of the Messenger of Allah and I will not invade the Ka'bah". So Yazid brought **Muslim b. Ukbe el-Murri**, an old and sick commander, at the head of the army. In Damascus, it was announced that each soldier would be given a full salary and a hundred dinars at once. Twelve thousand men ran to the call. As Yazid's army set out, he ordered Muslim: "Wait for them for three days. If they obey you, fight them whether they obey you or not. When you are victorious over them, let your army seize the city for three days. The goods, money, weapons and food in the city belong to the soldiers. Don't touch the crowd for three days". He ordered that if anything happened to him, **Husayn b. Numeyr** should take over the command of the army. In the same order, he also asked that no one should touch Zayn al-Abidin. The Prophet's city was promised as a three-day booty to the soldiers of the empire who killed his grandson.

scenes.2.text: Muslim motherfucker . Ukbe arrived in Medina in the last days of the month of Zilhicce, in the year 63 of the Hijrah. He camped his army east of the city in a place called Harre, covered in black volcanic rock. It was named after that black stone and went down in history as the Harre Affair. Muslims called for three days of obedience, as Yazid had ordered. The Medinans refused to submit again to a kingdom with the blood of the Prophet's grandson in its hands. When the battle began, the Medinese fought bravely. When the Syrian army saw the crowd and their stand, they were afraid. But at some point, there was a noise in the city. Damascus troops had entered the city from the neighborhood of Beni Harissa. The Medes, shot from behind, scattered. Abdullah b. Hanzala brought her sons forward one by one. Their sons were martyred before their eyes. In the end, he himself was martyred in battle. After the war, Muslim b. Ukbe, this is Mervan b. He walked among the dead with the judge. Abdullah b. Hanzala's witness finger was still in the air. When Marwan saw him, he said, "If you raised him when he was dead, you would have prayed with him a lot when he was alive". Among those martyred on that day were the companions of the Prophet. **Abdullah b. Zeyd**, who narrated the story of the Prophet, and **Ma'kil b. Sinân**, who carried the banner of his people in the conquest of Mecca, were among them.

scenes.3.text: When the war ended, Yazid's order was carried out. Muslim motherfucker . Ukbe made Medina lawful for his troops for three days. Soldiers break into houses, kill people and plunder. The women didn't get away with it either. According to Imam Malik, seven hundred people were killed on that day from the memory of the Quran. Even the Sunni historian Ibn Kathir called this command "a very great and ugly mistake". He wrote that in those three days, too many evils happened in Medina. The horses entered the Prophet's mosque and defiled the space between the tomb and the pulpit. The mosque of the Prophet is empty. Sayid b. He recalled those days: "There was no one in the mosque except me. The Damascenes would come in in groups and say, 'Look at this crazy old man.'" After three days, Muslim b. Ukba gathered the nobles of Medina. He asked them to pledge their allegiance to Yazid. According to this pact, Yazid would rule over their lives, their property and their families as he pleased. The one who tried to give the biat on the Prophet's circumcision was beaten in the neck. And not one was touched. When Umayyad's sons were expelled from Medina, Zaynab took Marwan's family under his protection. The imam, who even extended his arms to the family of his enemy, remained the face of the Ahl al-Bayt in Medina in those bloody days. The previous scholars swore that the commander who did this wrong was not a Muslim, but a "Musrif", that is, a transgressor.

scenes.4.text: The army that drenched Medina in blood, Abdullah b. He walked over to Zubair. Muslim motherfucker . And he died on the way to the place called Meshullah, and was buried there. At the head of the army, as ordered by Yazid, was Husayn b. Numeyr has passed. Husayn reached Mecca in the last days of Muharram and besieged the city for sixty-four days. In the 64th year of the Hijrah, on the third day of the month of Rabi'ul-Lev, the army of Damascus stoned the Kaaba with machetes and set it on fire. As the soldiers threw stones, they chanted, "We're throwing stones at the pillars of this mosque". The curtains of the Kaaba burned and the timber caught fire. A visitor found the Ka'bah uncovered and the cornerstone split in three. During the siege, Yazid died on the fourteenth of Rebiülevvel in the village of Huvvârîn near Humus. The news of his death reached Mecca at the beginning of the Last Day. The army broke off the siege and returned to Damascus. Yazid's reign lasted about three and a half years. In a short time, the Prophet's grandson was martyred in Karbala, the Prophet's city was sacked and the House of Allah was burned.

Numeir will besiege Mecca for sixty-four days. 3 Rebiülevvel 64 Saturday The Kaaba is stoned and burned with a machete; the cover and wood of the Kaaba burn, the cornerstone darkens and cracks in three places. Yazid died in Huvvârîn in 14 Rebiülevvel 64; his reign lasted three years six or eight months.

sunni.4.says: Abdullah b. Hanzala says he took Yazid's property to find strength to fight against him. From Bani Harise, the Damascenes enter the city, the Medinese disperse. He asks Muslims to pledge to be Yazid's servants. Ibn Kathir considers Yazid's making the city halal for three days "a great and ugly mistake"; he writes that many of his companions and sons were killed.
sunni.5.says: The delegation relates that Yazid drank wine and failed to make his prayers on time due to drunkenness; the Medina people lower him near the pulpit. His predecessor, Muslim b. Ukbe is called "Muzrif b. Ukbe", he said. From Imam Malik: In Harre, seven hundred people were killed for memorizing the Quran.
sunni.6.says: The Sahaba killed in Harre: Abdullah b. Hanzala (with eight sons), Abdullah b. Zeyd, this is Ma'kil b. It's a sign. Mervan's name is Abdullah b. What Hanzala said about the finger. Sayid b. That Musaeib is alone in the mosque. The people are being asked to pledge allegiance to Yazid.
sunni.7.says: From Kurtubi: the horses went around the mosque of the Prophet, defiled between the tomb and the pulpit.
shia.0.says: Yazid is fond of fun, birds of prey, dogs, monkeys, Persians and drinking parties; after the murder of Husayn, he sits with Ibn Ziyad at the drinking party.
shia.1.says: Three days of robbery and assault on women in Harre; horses from Kurtubi touring the mosque; Ibn Abi'l-Hadid to the fact that there is no worse incident in Islam than Harre; people being asked to be Yazid's slaves.
disputes.0.title: 1d6ihfw
Who burned the Kaaba?
disputes.0.sunni: Tabari writes that the Kaaba was stoned and burned with machetes. In the same place, a story from Waqidi relates that the fire was caused by the flame from the spear of one of Ibn Zubair's men, which was blown into the ceiling.
disputes.0.shia: It's Yazid's army that's setting up the siege, turning the manzikirs into the Kaaba and singing the song while throwing stones. The order to burn the house of God came from Damascus.
disputes.1.title: 10la4x6
The responsibility of Yazid
disputes.1.sunni: Ibn Kathir considers it a great and ugly mistake that Yazid made Medina lawful for three days. His predecessor, his commander, is Musrif b. It's called Ukbe.
disputes.1.shia: The three-day looting order is Yazid's own order. Karbala, Harre and Kaaba are the three great oppressions of the same kingdom.

summary: In 63 H, the people of Medina broke the pledge on the word of the delegation, seeing Yazid drinking wine and abandoning prayer. Yazid, the Muslim b. He ordered Ukbe to make the city halal for three days. In Harre, the Sahaba and their sons were killed, and the people were forced to be slaves to Yazid. She was not touched. In 64 H, Husayn b. Numeir besieged Mecca, the Kaaba was stoned and burned. Yazid died in the process. Common phrases are in Tabari 5/480-499 and al-Bid'ah.
key: On Yazid's orders, Medina was sacked for three days, and the Kaaba was stoned to death.
